newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: AMF sees full Kolwezi production in 2000.
newsitem.headline: AMF sees full Kolwezi production in 2000.

text.p: The Kolwezi copper/cobalt tailings project in the new Congo could produce 50,000 tonnes of copper a year and 6,000 tonnes of cobalt when it reaches full production in 2000, America Mineral Fields Inc said on Thursday.
"We would estimate at the moment that we'll be in production in the year 2000," AMF director Richard Garnett said in an interview.
U.S.-based AMF in April won the tender to develop Kolwezi as a joint venture with state mining company Gecamines. AMF has a 51 percent stake in the project.
Garnett said his company would likely spend between $200 million and $250 million to bring Kolwezi to full production.
"If you said of the order of $200 to $250 million that would be fine," Garnett said.
He said the Kolwezi tailings contained about 1.4 million tonnes of copper grading 1.34 percent and about 270,000 tonnes of cobalt grading 0.26 percent.
Garnett said about 92 percent of the copper could be recovered from the tailings and about 78 percent of the cobalt.
The project life is likely to be 27 years, he said.
Kolwezi will be one of the pivotal schemes to revitalise the country's mining industry, suffering from years of neglect under the rule of former president Mobutu Sese Seko.
Gecamines chairman Mbaka Kawaya told Reuters in Mauritius on Thursday that copper and cobalt output was likely to drop in 1997 from last year's production levels, but should increase in 1998.

The country remains one of the world's leading cobalt producers, accounting for around one fifth of supply, although annual production of around 5,000 tonnes is well down from the early 1980s when it was running at around 15,000.
Output of copper has slumped from 500,000 tonnes to around 40,000 tonnes.
